hints: The work done by the crane must supply both the gain in potential energy and the work done against resistance: $W = mgh + F_{\text{res}}d$.
Calculate work done against resistance: $25 \times 3.5 = 87.5\text{ J}$, and add the two quantities.
walkthrough: To raise the $50\text{ kg}$ block at constant speed, the crane must overcome both gravity and air resistance.

Calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy as the block is raised $h = 3.5\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 50 \times 10 \times 3.5 = 1750\text{ J}$$

Calculate the work done against the resistance force ($25\text{ N}$) over the vertical distance of $3.5\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = F_{\text{res}} \times h = 25 \times 3.5 = 87.5\text{ J}$$

The total work done by the crane is the sum of these two energies:
$$W = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{resistance}} = 1750 + 87.5 = 1837.5\text{ J}$$

hints: Power is the rate of doing work: $P = \frac{W}{t}$.
Substitute the total work done $W = 1837.5\text{ J}$ and time $t = 2\text{ s}$ to calculate the power.
walkthrough:
Power is defined as the rate at which work is done with respect to time:
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$

Substitute the total work done $W = 1837.5\text{ J}$ from part (i) and the time taken $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$P = \frac{1837.5}{2} = 918.75\text{ W} \approx 919\text{ W}$$
